notes: Draft: Stem: *capit-*. Languages: English, Spanish, Portuguese, French. About 120 entries, so the larger families may be trimmed to fit a puzzle of about 100.
Draft: *Capere* ("take": *capture, capable, accept, receive*) is a different root and the biggest trap in this family. None of those words belong here.
Draft: English *cap* and *cape* (cloak) come from Late Latin *cappa*, whose origin is uncertain, so they are excluded. *Cape* (headland) does come from *caput*.
Draft: *Caper* and *Capricorn* come from *caper* ("goat") and are excluded.
Draft: *Precipice* and *precipitate* come from *praeceps* (*prae* + *caput*, "headfirst"). This surprises players and makes a good reveal.

Draft: *Corporal* (rank) comes from Italian *caporale*, from *capo* ("head"); it is bonus-tier because it is easily confused with *corporal* (of the body). *Capitol* is bonus-tier because the origin of *Capitolium* is debated.
Draft: Spanish *jefe* and Portuguese *chefe* came through French *chef*.
Draft: To verify: *cabildo, caudillo* (from *capitellum*), *capataz, caboche, cheptel*, and English *cadet* and *caddie*.
